notes.bahari: Baharini: at sea, by the sea.
notes.jahazi: A large wooden sailing boat. Plural: majahazi.
notes.kaskazi: The wind that once brought traders from Arabia and India. Also “north”.
notes.kutoka-kiarabu: Many Swahili words come from Arabic: kitabu, saa, dunia.
notes.wenye: For people: watu wenye pesa. For an n- noun: yenye. For a town (mji): wenye.

guidebook.intro: Swahili grew in the trading towns of the East African coast, from Mogadishu to Sofala, where African, Arab, Persian and Indian worlds met.

tips.title: Things in the past
body: The past **-li-** takes the noun’s own prefix in front: **biashara ilikuwa kubwa** (trade was big), **kitabu kilikuwa** (the book was), **majahazi yalifika** (the dhows arrived).
People use **a-** and **wa-**: **wafanyabiashara walifika** (the traders arrived).

tips.title: -enye: with, having
body: **-enye** means “having” or “with”, and agrees with its noun: **mji wenye historia** (a town with history), **watu wenye pesa** (people with money), **nyumba yenye vyumba vitatu** (a house with three rooms).

culture.title: A Bantu language with many borrowings
body: Swahili is a Bantu language, a cousin of Luganda and Kikuyu, but its traders borrowed freely: **kitabu** and **saa** from Arabic, **chai** from Persian and Hindi, **meza** from Portuguese, **baiskeli** from English.

culture.title: The dhow
body: Wooden **majahazi** still sail between Zanzibar, Lamu and the mainland. For centuries they followed the monsoon: south with the **kaskazi**, home again with the **kusi**.
